concepts.definition: Standard is a pay-as-you-go deployment type that scales with request demand without reserving provisioned throughput units (PTUs). Unlike Global Standard, processing stays within the deployment's Azure geography, so it fits the EU data-residency requirement.
Global Standard can route inference traffic across supported global regions. That conflicts with the requirement that model processing remain within the EU.
Global Provisioned uses reserved provisioned throughput and can route processing globally. The scenario explicitly requires dynamic scaling without reserved throughput and requires EU data residency.
Serverless API is the broader Foundry deployment option under which pay-per-token deployment types are exposed. The question asks specifically for the deployment type, not the deployment option.
Batch is asynchronous and optimized for offline high-throughput jobs, so it does not meet the real-time inference requirement.
A self-hosted/managed-compute container uses dedicated compute capacity and therefore conflicts with the requirement to avoid subscription VM/vCPU capacity.
An LLM is designed for long-context natural-language generation and multi-step reasoning. An SLM prioritizes efficiency, while multimodal and key-phrase models solve different tasks.
An SLM offers lower latency and cost with reduced capacity. It can handle simpler tasks, but it is not the best fit for the required context-aware generation and complex reasoning.
An embedding model converts documents and queries into numeric vectors whose distance represents semantic similarity. Those vectors are what the search solution requires.
A multimodal model processes combinations such as text and images. The scenario only requires grounded natural-language support responses, so multimodal capability is not the deciding requirement.
An image-generation model creates images from prompts or reference media. It does not encode policy text into vectors for search.
A speech-to-text model used to transcribe spoken audio into text.
Fine-tuning changes a model's learned behavior using training examples. It is a model-improvement technique, not a measurement of whether a particular response is grounded in supplied sources.
A routing pattern that sends simpler requests to a cheaper model and escalates harder requests to a more capable model.
File Search indexes files attached or uploaded for the agent and retrieves relevant passages from them. It matches the requirement to answer from documents uploaded directly to the agent.
Code Interpreter gives the agent a sandboxed Python execution environment for calculations and data processing. It is the tool designed for performing computations during a conversation.
Azure AI Search retrieves content from a separately managed Search index. The scenario's curated files can be grounded directly with the agent's file-search capability instead.

Grounding with Bing Search lets an agent retrieve current public web information and use it as grounding. It matches the requirement for up-to-date information from public websites; File Search targets uploaded files and Code Interpreter executes code.
A tool that lets an agent interact with a graphical user interface by observing the screen and taking actions.
A Foundry workflow provides deterministic steps, conditional branches, shared state, and optional actions without requiring custom orchestration code.
A collaboration pattern in which multiple agents share a conversation and control can pass between them.
An orchestration pattern that passes the output of one step or agent to the next in a fixed order.
An orchestration pattern that pauses execution for human input, review, or approval.
Conversation history retains messages inside one conversation. It does not automatically remember preferences across separate conversations.
Session context preserves state managed by the current orchestration session. It is temporary and not durable cross-conversation memory.
Persistent memory that lets an agent reuse relevant information across separate conversations.

RAG retrieves external information at run time and adds it as grounding context. The task instead asks to demonstrate the desired classification behavior with labeled examples inside the prompt, so retrieval is unnecessary.

Classic RAG typically performs a retrieval step from the user's query and then sends retrieved chunks to the model. It lacks the agentic query decomposition, conversation-aware planning, and parallel subquery execution required here.
Agentic RAG can decompose a complex request into parallel subqueries, use conversation context to plan retrieval, and combine evidence from multiple chunks.

Iterative retrieval performs repeated retrieval passes, but by itself it does not provide the conversational query planning, decomposition, and parallel subquery execution described in the requirements.
Vector search compares embeddings and retrieves content by semantic similarity even when the query and document use different wording.
Lexical retrieval that matches words and terms in the query against indexed text.
Hybrid search combines lexical and vector retrieval, allowing exact product identifiers and semantically similar descriptions to contribute to the result set.
Search enhanced by language understanding; in Azure AI Search, semantic ranker reranks an initial text result set.
Semantic ranking reranks an existing text result set for relevance. It improves ranking but still needs an initial keyword or vector retrieval method.
Suggesters provide type-ahead and autocomplete suggestions from configured text fields. They are not used for semantic document retrieval in RAG.
Analyzers tokenize and normalize text during indexing and querying. They support lexical search but do not create embedding-based semantic similarity.

Azure OpenAI Embedding converts each text chunk into a numeric embedding vector. Azure AI Search stores those vectors so vector queries can retrieve semantically similar chunks even when wording differs.
Text Split divides long document text into smaller pages/chunks that fit retrieval and embedding limits. Smaller retrieval-sized chunks improve the granularity of Azure AI Search retrieval.
The Merge skill combines text or inserted content into one field. It does not perform OCR or split long content for indexing.
Entity Recognition finds named entities such as people, organizations, and locations. It does not extract image text or divide long document text into searchable chunks.
Language Detection identifies the language of text. It is useful for multilingual processing but does not satisfy the OCR and chunking requirements here.
Key phrase extraction identifies important phrases in existing text. It does not read scanned images or create appropriately sized search chunks.
An Azure AI Search skill that restructures enriched data into a new complex shape.
A component that reads content from a data source and populates or refreshes a search index.
Microsoft's Azure platform for building, evaluating, deploying, and operating AI applications and agents.
Azure AI Search supplies the private-document index and supports semantic and vector retrieval. Extraction services can prepare content but do not replace the search layer.
Azure Content Understanding produces multimodal document representations with source grounding for text and visual regions, supporting the requested page-level citations and polygons.
A document AI service for OCR, layout analysis, and structured field extraction.
Azure services for language tasks such as text analysis, entity recognition, and classification.
An Azure service for machine translation of text and documents.
Image Analysis describes visual features such as objects, tags, and captions. It is not optimized for structured invoice fields and document tables.

Application Insights is Azure Monitor's application observability backend for requests, dependencies, exceptions, performance data, and distributed traces. It can receive and visualize the agent application's trace data, so it is one of the two appropriate components.

A Log Analytics workspace stores and queries logs that resources send to it, but it does not by itself instrument a Python agent application or create end-to-end LLM/tool spans. Additional telemetry instrumentation/export is still required.

Microsoft Sentinel is a SIEM/SOAR service for security analytics and incident response. It can consume logs, but it is not the application-tracing instrumentation or backend used to capture agent latency breakdowns and exceptions.
OCR converts printed text in the scanned invoice images into machine-readable text that can be mapped into searchable index fields.
Document Extraction extracts document content and fields, but it is not the single multimodal Search skill that produces page-level text and image locations with bounding polygons.
Document Layout focuses on page structure and text layout. The multimodal extraction skill is required when citations must cover both text and images with locations.

OCR or the prebuilt-read analyzer extracts printed and handwritten text, but does not preserve the full document structure needed for layout-aware processing. The prebuilt-layout analyzer extracts text together with structural elements such as tables, selection marks, and document layout.
The prebuilt-layout model extracts structural elements such as tables and can detect barcodes and QR codes; prebuilt-read focuses on OCR text.
The prebuilt document-search analyzer produces retrieval-oriented content that preserves useful document structure and links for downstream agent grounding.

Standard mode is designed for high-volume, cost-effective analysis of a single file. Pipeline1 processes standalone PDF invoices and does not require cross-document reasoning or reference data, so a single-file task in standard mode is appropriate.
An advanced Content Understanding task for analyzing one document with greater reasoning capability.

Pro mode adds advanced multi-step reasoning and support for multiple files/reference data. Pipeline2 must compare information across documents and validate it against reference data, so it needs a multi-file task in pro mode.
File projection writes binary or file-like enrichment outputs to blob storage. Unstructured JSON is better preserved as an object.
Object projection stores a hierarchical JSON object and preserves the structure of unstructured enrichment data.
Table projection flattens data into rows and columns in Azure Table Storage. It is not the best match for preserving arbitrary nested JSON.
An Azure-managed identity whose lifecycle is tied to the resource on which it is enabled.
A user-assigned managed identity can represent Azure workloads, but a GitHub-hosted runner signs in to Azure through federated OIDC rather than directly using managed identity metadata.

DefaultAzureCredential is an Azure Identity credential chain that can obtain Microsoft Entra tokens from a managed identity when the app runs on an Azure host with managed identity enabled. It avoids storing API keys or client secrets, so it meets the managed-identity requirement.
ClientSecretCredential uses a tenant ID, client ID, and stored client secret. It is an application credential, not managed identity authentication.
AzureKeyCredential authenticates with a static service key. It cannot satisfy the requirement to use a Microsoft Entra managed identity.
AccountManagedIdentity tells the connection to authenticate as the Foundry account's managed identity without storing a secret.
AccountKey authenticates with a shared account key. Key Vault access in this design uses the Foundry account's managed identity instead.
ApiKey represents an API-key credential. Azure Key Vault uses Microsoft Entra authorization for this managed-identity connection.
Authentication succeeded, so the 403 indicates missing data-plane authorization. Cognitive Services OpenAI User grants model inference with less privilege than Contributor.
Cognitive Services User grants data-plane access to supported Azure AI services generally. Azure OpenAI inference requires the OpenAI-specific user role in this scenario.
Cognitive Services Data Reader is intended for reading service data and metadata. It does not grant permission to invoke an Azure OpenAI model deployment.
Contributor manages Azure resources in the control plane, such as creating or changing deployments. It does not by itself grant Azure OpenAI data-plane inference access.
An Azure data-plane role that allows an identity to read blob data.
An Azure data-plane role that allows an identity to read, write, and delete blob data.
An Azure data-plane role that allows an identity to read and modify queue data.
An Azure role that allows an identity to read secret values from Azure Key Vault.
An OpenAPI apiKey security scheme declares where the header key belongs and lets the tool inject the value from the configured project connection.
A bearer security scheme sends a token in the Authorization header. The weather service expects an API key in its own header, so an apiKey security scheme is required instead.
An Azure Key Vault connection can provide secure access to secrets, but the OpenAPI document still needs an apiKey security scheme so the tool knows where to place the credential.
An authentication pattern that forwards the caller's Microsoft Entra identity to an underlying tool or API.
A separate identity assigned to a published agent or client so its tool access is isolated and auditable.
A project-level identity that can be shared by multiple agents or clients.
Groundedness measures whether statements in the response are supported by the supplied context, making it a core RAG evaluation metric.
Measures how directly and appropriately a response addresses the user's request or intended task.
Fluency measures grammatical quality and readability of the generated response. A response can be fluent even when retrieval is poor or claims are unsupported.
Coherence measures whether the response is logically organized and internally consistent. It does not directly test retrieval quality or source support.
Response Completeness measures whether the answer covers required information. It does not specifically assess whether retrieval found the right evidence or whether claims are grounded.
Groundedness evaluation checks whether generated claims are supported by the retrieved source material. RAG evaluation is broader and fine-tuning does not directly measure factual support.
RAG retrieves external source content and supplies it as grounding context before generation. Groundedness evaluation checks whether generated claims are supported by the supplied source context.
The fluency evaluator measures language quality and readability. It does not provide groundedness, relevance, or harmful-content category scores.
Similarity evaluators compare generated and reference text using lexical or embedding similarity. They are not the evaluation category for RAG groundedness and safety.

Risk and safety metrics evaluate harmful or policy-violating content categories. They are the relevant signal for responses flagged for policy violations; latency and token metrics instead measure performance or usage.
Prompt Shields detect direct and indirect prompt-injection attempts. They protect model instructions, but they do not perform PII detection or redaction.

Prompt Shields for User Prompts inspect instructions supplied directly by the user as the prompt. Here the risky text is appended as external OCR/document context, so the document/indirect-attack shield is the appropriate scope instead.

Prompt Shields for Documents inspect third-party or retrieved text for indirect prompt-injection instructions. Because the OCR result is appended as untrusted contextual text, the document shield is the control that targets the stated attack.
PII Detection identifies sensitive personal information so it can be removed or blocked before customer data is exposed. Content-category filters and Prompt Shields address different risks.

Self-harm content filtering detects and optionally blocks text associated with self-harm at configured severity levels. It does not identify or redact personal data such as names, addresses, or account numbers.
Violence content filtering classifies violent content and can block it by severity. It does not detect the personal information required by this compliance scenario.

Image moderation classifies harmful visual content such as violence or sexual content. The problem here is not visual harm; it is malicious instructions contained in OCR-extracted text, so image moderation addresses a different risk.

Protected material detection looks for known protected text or code that the model may reproduce. It does not generally detect arbitrary confidential, proprietary, or personally identifiable information. Therefore it is only correct if the question's 'sensitive or proprietary information' specifically means protected/copyrighted material.
Indirect attack detects malicious instructions embedded in retrieved content. It addresses prompt injection, not copyrighted or protected material.
A custom guardrail validates or constrains inputs, outputs, or tool behavior according to a policy. It does not specifically score whether every generated claim is supported by retrieved evidence.
Fairness concerns equitable treatment and avoiding systematic performance differences across groups. Informing users that their data is processed is not primarily a fairness control.
Transparency requires communicating how and when an AI system is used, including notifying users that their submitted data is being processed.
Inclusiveness focuses on designing systems that empower people with different abilities and backgrounds. User notification is more directly an issue of transparency.
Reliability and safety concern consistent operation, robustness, and harm prevention. A processing notice explains system use rather than improving technical reliability.

Tracing exposes the ordered spans, tool calls, model calls, exceptions, and latency for one run, making it suitable for diagnosing both slow execution and incorrect reasoning after correct tool output.

A trace is made of spans that represent individual operations. Hierarchical parent/child spans preserve the nested structure of an agent run, so model calls, agent handoffs, and tool calls can be audited in their execution context.

Tool-call span attributes are metadata fields attached to tool invocation spans. They can record the tool name plus invocation arguments and returned results, which is the metadata required for auditing tool use.

OpenTelemetry provides the instrumentation, span model, and exporters used to trace the Python service's model and tool operations. Those spans can be exported to Application Insights to provide end-to-end tracing outside the Foundry portal.
Token analytics separates input, output, and tool-related token consumption, allowing a cost increase to be diagnosed even when request volume is unchanged.
Latency measures how long requests, model calls, and tool calls take. It helps diagnose performance delays, not a cost increase when traffic volume is unchanged.
Run success rate shows the proportion of runs that complete successfully. Costs can rise while the success rate and request count remain unchanged.
A metric that measures how often a model or deployment is available to serve requests.
A metric that shows how much of the reserved model capacity is being used.
RequestResponse logging captures model request and response diagnostics needed to investigate failed or unexpected inference calls.
A rule that controls which traces, or what proportion of traces, are collected.
Transcribes streaming speech into text with low latency.
Transcribes prerecorded audio files asynchronously in batch jobs.
Synthesizes spoken audio from written text.
Recognizes spoken input and translates it into another language.
A neural text-to-speech voice trained for a specific voice identity and approved use case.
Markup used to control speech synthesis details such as pronunciation, pauses, rate, pitch, and emphasis.
The project property must identify the Custom Speech project that owns the fine-tuned model. A Foundry project ID or endpoint URL identifies a different resource.
The custom endpoint URL is the address used to send recognition requests to a deployed model. It is not the project identifier requested by this API field.

WebRTC is designed for interactive client-side audio/video and is Microsoft's recommended GPT Realtime transport for web and mobile clients. Microsoft lists it as the lowest-latency option (about 50–100 ms), so it matches a browser app targeting roughly 100 ms latency.

WebSocket is supported by GPT Realtime, but Microsoft recommends it mainly for server-to-server scenarios where the lowest latency is not required. Its documented latency is higher (roughly 100–300 ms) than WebRTC, so it does not best meet the browser/~100 ms requirement.
SIP is a telephony signaling protocol intended for phone-system integration. It is a supported Realtime connection method for telephony, not the best choice for a browser web app.
RTMP is a media streaming protocol commonly used for live video delivery or ingest, but it is not one of the GPT Realtime API connection methods documented by Microsoft.
An SDK options object that specifies the text and categories used in a Content Safety text-analysis request.
An SDK enum value representing the self-harm category in Content Safety analysis.
Few-shot prompting includes representative labeled examples so the model can imitate the required support-ticket classifications without retraining.
Zero-shot prompting gives instructions without examples. It relies on the model to infer the desired label format and therefore does not meet the requirement to show correct classifications.
Chain-of-thought is a reasoning/prompting concept, not a retrieval architecture. It does not connect the application to Azure AI Search or run parallel retrieval queries.
The process of selecting the next token from a model's probability distribution.
Limits token selection to the smallest candidate set whose cumulative probability reaches p.
A parameter that controls how concentrated or varied the model's token probabilities are.
A parameter that can reduce the likelihood of repeating concepts that have already appeared.
The maximum number of tokens the model is allowed to generate in its response.
Sequences that cause the model to stop generating when they are encountered.
A value that can make sampling more reproducible when the model and API support it.
High-priority instructions that define the model's overall role, behavior, and constraints.
An identity layer built on OAuth 2.0 that supports federated authentication and ID tokens.
A token used for delegated or application access under the OAuth authorization framework.
A PAT is a stored GitHub secret with a lifecycle and broad misuse risk. OIDC allows the workflow to obtain short-lived Azure credentials without storing a cloud secret.
A time-limited, permission-scoped token that delegates access to Azure Storage resources.
A service key used to authenticate requests to an Azure service endpoint.
Storage access keys are long-lived shared secrets. They violate the requirement for identity-based, keyless access.
A digital certificate that can authenticate an application or service instead of using a client secret.
Image editing that regenerates only the area selected by a mask.
A generation mode that uses an existing image as the visual starting point.
A generation mode that creates an image from a text prompt.
A generation mode that creates a new variation of a reference image.
A parameter that controls how strongly an image edit preserves characteristics of the input image.
A parameter that controls how strongly image generation follows the prompt.
A model-assisted metric that judges similarity between generated output and a reference or target answer.
The harmonic mean of precision and recall: 2 × precision × recall / (precision + recall).
A text-similarity metric that measures overlap between generated text and reference text.
Prediction drift measures changes in a predictive model's data or behavior over time. Azure AI Search relevance is diagnosed with search and retrieval evaluation metrics instead.
AI-assisted quality metrics use an evaluator model to judge qualities such as groundedness and relevance. They supply the requested RAG quality scores.
AI quality NLP metrics are traditional text metrics and evaluators. The requested groundedness and relevance measures are AI-assisted quality evaluators rather than only NLP similarity metrics.
A numeric estimate of how certain a model, analysis, or extraction is about its result.
An Azure AI Search relevance score assigned to a result for a specific query.
An Azure AI Search key with restricted permission to run queries against indexes.
An Azure AI Search key with broad data-plane administrative access.
The current execution state and most recent result of an Azure AI Search indexer.
A record of failures that occurred during previous indexer runs.
Indexer settings that map enriched skill outputs to fields in the target search index.
A collection of normalized page-image objects created during Azure AI Search document enrichment.
A collection of Azure AI Search skills executed as an enrichment pipeline during indexing.
Immersive Reader provides reading aids such as text spacing, line focus, syllables, picture dictionary, and read-aloud, directly supporting users with dyslexia and comprehension differences.
Microsoft's integrated platform for data engineering, analytics, data science, and business intelligence.
An API for accessing Microsoft 365 and Microsoft Entra resources and data.
An Azure platform for training, registering, deploying, and managing machine-learning models.
Azure Monitor Agent collects operating-system and guest telemetry from supported machines. It does not instrument LLM calls, tool calls, or agent-run spans inside this Python application.
A local runtime and development environment for supported Foundry models and workflows.
Text Translation converts already extracted text between languages. It does not perform OCR on scanned invoices.
Translates complete documents while preserving their structure and formatting where possible.
`TextAnalytics` creates a Language-specific resource. It cannot also provide OCR/vision through the same account.
LanguageAuthoring is used for authoring Azure Language projects such as classification or NER. It does not host the required generative model.
Custom lists of terms or phrases that a safety system should identify and block.
A technique that marks external text as untrusted data so a model can distinguish it from instructions.
Hateful and unfair content detects discriminatory or hateful language. It does not detect copied protected text or code.
Violent content detects descriptions or depictions of violence. It is unrelated to protected-text or protected-code detection.
A safety control that identifies generated claims that are unsupported by the supplied source context.
The agent definition contains instructions, model settings, and tools shared across users. It should not be used as the state container for one customer's case.
A conversation stores the ordered messages and outputs for a continuing interaction, allowing the same support case to resume across requests.

A session-specific scope can prevent cross-session memory only when the application supplies a different scope value for every session. The literal value `session` alone would be a shared static partition, which is why the wording is ambiguous.
A legacy Agents/Assistants pattern in which a thread stores messages and a run executes an agent against that state.
Chat completions generate or reason over text supplied in a prompt. They are not the specialized document-analysis capability for extracting invoice fields and layout.
An API for model responses that supports multimodal input, tools, and a unified structured response format.
An output item is one piece of content produced during a response, such as a message or tool call. It does not represent the persistent multi-turn support case.
Kusto Query Language, used to query log, telemetry, and analytics data in Azure.
An SDK method that submits an image for analysis and returns visual analysis results.
An SDK method that submits text for analysis and returns language-analysis results.
A project container for models, deployments, agents, connections, evaluations, and related resources.
A managed service for creating, publishing, and running agents with models, instructions, knowledge, and tools.
An agent whose behavior is defined by a model, instructions, and configured knowledge or tools.
A versioned agent that has been published so applications or workflows can invoke it.
The model returns a structured function request with arguments; the application executes it and sends back the result.
An application-defined function exposed to an agent with a name, description, and argument schema.
A tool that lets an agent call HTTP operations described by an OpenAPI specification.
Model Context Protocol, a standard protocol for exposing tools, resources, and prompts to AI clients.
A server that exposes tools, resources, or prompts through Model Context Protocol.
An invokable capability described and exposed by an MCP server.
A client that connects to MCP servers, discovers their capabilities, and invokes their tools.
Allows the model to decide whether a tool needs to be used.
Requires the model to make at least one tool call before completing the response.
Prevents the model from using tools for the request.
Forces the model to use the specified tool or tool type.
Pauses a workflow or tool call until a person approves or rejects the action.
A workflow node that requires a human decision before a sensitive next step can run.
Evaluates a condition and selects which branch of a workflow should execute.
A workflow node that collects an answer or approval from a person.
Stores user- or task-specific information that can be retrieved in later conversations.
Persistent storage in which agent memories are saved and searched.
An agent tool that searches for relevant entries in a configured memory store.
A partition key that determines which memories a run can save and retrieve, such as one scope per user.
Defines where indexable content is located and how an Azure AI Search indexer connects to it.
A searchable schema containing fields and documents against which queries run.
Splits long content into smaller units that can be indexed and retrieved separately.
Repeats some text between neighboring chunks to preserve context across boundaries.
Splits content after a fixed number of tokens or characters regardless of document structure.
Splits content at headings, paragraphs, tables, or other structural boundaries.
An Azure data-plane role that allows an identity to read and query documents in search indexes.
An Azure data-plane role that allows an identity to add, update, and delete documents in search indexes.
An Azure control-plane role for managing a Search service without automatically granting access to index data.
Assigns an Azure PaaS service a private IP address inside a virtual network.
A private endpoint created and managed from one managed Azure service to another resource.
A connection that uses Microsoft Entra identity and RBAC instead of a stored API key.
Role-Based Access Control, which assigns roles to identities at a defined Azure scope.
A configuration that defines the input modality, schema, and analysis used to produce structured output.
A ready-made analyzer for a common scenario that does not require defining the full field schema.
An analyzer with a user-defined schema for the fields a solution needs to extract or generate.
The definition of field names, data types, descriptions, and generation methods in analyzer output.
A field whose value the model generates or derives from the content according to its schema and instructions.
A field whose value is selected from predefined categories through classification.
An estimate of how certain the analyzer is about an extracted field value.
A reference to the location in the source content that supports an extracted field value.
An Azure service that classifies and can filter harmful text and image content in supported categories.
A custom list of terms that should be detected in addition to built-in safety classifiers.
Identifies claims in generated output that are unsupported by the supplied context.
Creates a new Responses API request using the specified model, input, and tools.
Retrieves a previously stored response object by its ID.
Compacts conversation state to reduce the amount of history that must be carried forward.
A convenience property that collects the text output from a Responses API response.
Retrieves an existing agent definition or agent resource.
Retrieves a specific published version of an agent.
Creates or publishes a new version of an agent definition.
Starts an agent run and processes it until it reaches a completed or waiting state.
Starts an asynchronous video-generation job.
Retrieves the current status and metadata of a video-generation job.
Downloads the generated video bytes after the job completes.
Shows whether a video-generation job is queued, running, completed, or failed.
The SDK client used to call an Azure AI Content Safety endpoint.
Sends a text-analysis request to Content Safety and returns category results.

`--assign-identity` enables a managed identity on the Cognitive Services/OpenAI resource. That identity is needed for Key Vault access, but this switch does not take the encryption JSON shown in the next line.

`--encryption` accepts the customer-managed-key configuration containing `keySource: Microsoft.KeyVault` and `keyVaultProperties`. Microsoft’s CLI example enables the managed identity with `--assign-identity` and then supplies the Key Vault encryption configuration with `--encryption`.
Specifies the type of Cognitive Services resource to create, such as OpenAI.
Specifies the pricing or capacity tier of the resource.
Allows a deployment to move to a newer default model version under the service's automatic upgrade policy.
Keeps the current model version until it is retired, then upgrades the deployment.

concepts.term: Upgrade when new default is available
concepts.definition: Upgrades the deployment when a new default model version becomes available.
Keeps an explicitly selected model version and requires future version changes to be managed manually.
A subscription- and region-specific limit on how much of a model or service can be deployed or consumed.
A limit on how many requests or tokens can be processed during a time interval.
Reserved model capacity purchased in PTUs to provide more predictable throughput.
Bad Request: the request is invalid, for example because of malformed input or an exceeded input limit.
Unauthorized: authentication is missing or the credential or token is invalid.
Forbidden: the identity is authenticated but does not have the required permission.
Too Many Requests: the service rate limit or available quota has been exceeded.
Another attempt made after a temporary failure that may succeed later.
Increases the waiting time between retries to reduce load and repeated collisions.
Adds random variation to retry delays so many clients do not retry at the same moment.
The service limits request throughput when a client exceeds capacity or rate limits.
The proportion of reported positive detections that are correct: TP / (TP + FP).
The proportion of actual positive objects the model finds: TP / (TP + FN).
Mean Average Precision, which summarizes detection precision across classes and often multiple confidence or IoU thresholds.
Intersection over Union, the overlap between predicted and actual bounding boxes divided by their union.
A reported detection that correctly matches a real object under the evaluation rule.
A reported detection that should not count as a correct match.
A real object that the model fails to detect.
The minimum confidence score required for a prediction to be counted or displayed.
A legacy Azure service for training custom image-classification and object-detection models.
A vision feature that identifies known brands or logos and can return their name, confidence, and region.
A rectangular region that locates an object using coordinates and dimensions.
A set of points describing the more exact position and shape of a region in a document or image.
Marks a content item as text in a multimodal message array.
Marks a content item as an image reference that the model should process visually.
Base64-encoded image data embedded in a data URL where the API supports image URL input.
The field containing an image URL or supported data URL in an image content item.
An SDK enum value that requests Markdown as the text format for document-analysis output.
A parameter that specifies the text format used in Document Intelligence results.
Requests figure output so detected figures can be returned or downloaded.
Requests Markdown format in a supported REST or tool call for document analysis.
A kind value that selects personally identifiable information entity recognition.
A list specifying which types of personally identifiable information the analysis should target.
A redaction policy that replaces detected PII entities with a mask.
The result field containing the text after detected PII has been masked.
IsBlank(Local.Var01) is true when the local variable has no value. The workflow needs the opposite condition so it continues after the user supplied an answer.
IsEmpty is intended for an empty table or collection in Power Fx. Var01 stores one response value, so IsBlank is the appropriate test.
Not(IsBlank(Local.Var01)) is true only after the local response variable contains a value, allowing the next step to run.
Returns the text value of Local.Var01 converted to uppercase.
References an Azure resource that already exists without attempting to create it again.
Specifies the parent resource of a nested Bicep resource.
Specifies the subscription, resource group, or resource at which a Bicep declaration is resolved or deployed.
A Bicep function that returns information about the current or specified resource group.
Creates or replaces a resource at a known Azure Resource Manager URI.
Updates selected properties of an existing resource.
An Azure namespace that owns a resource type, such as Microsoft.CognitiveServices.
The version of an Azure Resource Manager resource contract that controls available properties and behavior.

`{{$userId}}` is the special scope value that Foundry resolves to the end user's identity. It intentionally preserves a user's memory across separate conversations, so it is the opposite of session-only isolation.
A shared memory scope in which memories are not isolated by user and therefore require special care.
The name of the memory store that MemorySearchTool should use.
A rule that blocks the next delivery step when defined quality requirements are not met.
A minimum or maximum allowed metric value that determines whether an evaluation passes.
GitHub rules that can require successful status checks before changes are merged into a branch.
Lets a workflow obtain short-lived Azure tokens without storing a long-lived client secret.
